passage: When I left the tutoring collective, I promised myself two things: say it honestly, and finish what I had already agreed to. Harsha here. I told Jaya, who runs the collective, that I was leaving because my new job's hours no longer fit, and that nobody had done anything wrong. I asked what was still pending, and we wrote a list: the March workshop, two parent calls and the fee register. I finished all three before my last day. I did not complain about the timetable mess in the group chat, even though I could have. On my last evening Jaya said, "The door is open." A month later a former colleague asked me for a reference, and I said yes without hesitation.

qa.q: What three things did Harsha finish before the last day?
qa.a: Harsha finished the March workshop, two parent calls and the fee register.

qa.q: What did Harsha want the departure to be like?
qa.a: Honest and responsible, with Harsha feeling determined to finish the commitments already made and not blame anyone.

qa.q: Why did Harsha choose not to complain in the group chat?
qa.a: Complaining could burn bridges, and leaving without blame keeps trust and reputation.

qa.q: How might Jaya feel about the way Harsha left?
qa.a: Probably respected and reassured, since Harsha gave an honest reason and Jaya said the door is open.

grounding: Illustrates a person who leaves a role honestly, finishes commitments already made and does not burn bridges.

passage: Head coach's note, Salma. Saurabh told me on the second of the month that he is leaving the club to take a night-shift job, and he gave a month. He explained plainly that the hours no longer worked and blamed nobody. He asked to keep the under-14 team through the district tournament, and did, arriving on time to every session. He wrote a one-page plan for each player and handed the kit list and bus bookings to Devika. On his last day he told the children himself and thanked the parents in person. Two parents asked whether the club had quarrelled, and Saurabh said no, in front of them. I would happily give him a reference.

qa.q: Which team did Saurabh keep through the district tournament?
qa.a: Saurabh kept the under-14 team.

qa.q: What does Saurabh's behaviour suggest he felt toward the children and the club?
qa.a: Saurabh seems to have felt caring and protective toward the children and loyal to the club, since he told the children himself and did not leave them without a plan.

qa.q: What could another person leaving a team copy from Saurabh?
qa.a: State the reason plainly, finish agreed tasks, write a handover and avoid blaming anyone.

qa.q: How might the parents have felt after hearing Saurabh's answer?
qa.a: Reassured that nothing was wrong at the club, since he told them plainly there had been no quarrel.

grounding: Illustrates a person who leaves cleanly by giving notice, finishing commitments, handing over and not blaming, and earns a good reference.

passage:
Sunday night.
Told the band today that I'm leaving after the Diwali gig.
I've been thinking about it for months. I love them, but with my new job I miss half the practices, and I hate being the one who's always late with new songs. It's not fair to them.
I almost just stopped replying to the group, the way Karan did last year. We never really forgave him.
Instead I asked Trisha to meet me for coffee first, since she started the band. I said it straight: I'm leaving, it's my schedule, not anyone's fault. I'll play the Diwali gig, all four songs, and I'll help teach my parts to whoever replaces me.
She was quiet, then said, "Honestly, I guessed. Thank you for telling me properly."
Then I told the rest at practice. Nobody was angry. Rohit asked if I'd come to the gig after that as audience. I said yes.
I'm Himani, and this is the first time I've left something without feeling like I ran away.

qa.q: After which gig is the narrator leaving the band?
qa.a: After the Diwali gig.

qa.q: How does Himani feel about the way this ending went?
qa.a: Himani feels relieved and at peace, for once not feeling like running away.

qa.q: What did Himani do that made this a clean exit?
qa.a: Himani told Trisha first and in person, gave an honest reason without blame, committed to the Diwali gig and offered to teach the parts.

qa.q: How did Trisha react to the news?
qa.a: Trisha was quiet but grateful, saying she had guessed and thanking Himani for telling her properly.

grounding: Illustrates a person who leaves a band honestly, finishes commitments and avoids blame, protecting relationships and reputation.

passage:
Ujjwal: Hi Jyoti, do you have 10 mins today? It's about the website project
Jyoti: Sure, call at 4?
Ujjwal: Actually I'd like to say it in writing first, then call
Ujjwal: I've accepted a full-time role starting in February. So I'll be stepping away from freelance work after this project
Jyoti: Oh! Congratulations. But what about our launch?
Ujjwal: The launch is on 20 Jan. I'll finish everything I promised before that: the booking page, the payment flow and testing
Ujjwal: I'll also write up how everything works, so whoever maintains it later isn't lost
Jyoti: That's a relief honestly 😅
Jyoti: I was worried you'd disappear like the last developer
Ujjwal: No. You trusted me with this. I want to finish it properly
Jyoti: Can I still call you if something breaks in March?
Ujjwal: For a short question, yes, of course 🙂
Jyoti: Then congratulations for real. Talk at 4

qa.q: When is the launch?
qa.a: The launch is on 20 Jan.

qa.q: Why did Ujjwal want to say it in writing first?
qa.a: Ujjwal felt nervous and responsible, wanting the news and the plan to be clear before the call.

qa.q: What makes Ujjwal's exit clean?
qa.a: Ujjwal tells Jyoti early and honestly, promises to finish everything already committed, writes up how it works and stays open for short questions.

qa.q: How does Jyoti feel once the plan is clear?
qa.a: Jyoti feels relieved, having worried Ujjwal would disappear like the last developer, and ends up congratulating Ujjwal for real.

grounding: Shows a freelancer who ends a project cleanly by telling the client honestly, finishing commitments and leaving good documentation.

passage:
Dolma had taught at the small school in Ravangla for two years. In March she accepted a place in a teacher training college in Siliguri. The new term there began in July.
She didn't tell the children first, or post it anywhere. She went to the headmaster, Mohit sir, one morning before assembly. "Sir, I'm leaving at the end of this term. I wanted you to know first, with enough time."
He was quiet. The school had few teachers. "It will be hard to replace you."
"I know. I'll finish the syllabus for both my classes. I'll leave lesson plans for the first month. And if you find someone by May, I'll let them sit in my classes."
He found a young teacher from Namchi in May. Dolma had her teach alongside for three weeks.
On her last day, the children gave her a card. Mohit sir said at assembly, "Ms Dolma is not leaving us. She is going ahead." She tried very hard not to cry, and failed.

qa.q: When did Mohit sir find a new teacher?
qa.a: He found a young teacher from Namchi in May.

qa.q: How did Dolma feel on her last day?
qa.a: Dolma felt moved and sad, trying hard not to cry and failing.

qa.q: What did Dolma do that made her leaving clean?
qa.a: She told the headmaster first with enough time, finished the syllabus, left lesson plans and let her replacement teach alongside her.

qa.q: How does Mohit sir see Dolma's leaving by the end?
qa.a: Mohit sir sees it with respect and warmth, saying she is going ahead rather than leaving them.

grounding: Illustrates a teacher who leaves a school honestly, finishes commitments and trains a replacement, leaving without burning bridges.

passage:
Mina had worked at Priscila's bakery in São Paulo for two years when a hotel kitchen offered her a pastry job. She told Priscila first, before anyone else, on a quiet Tuesday morning while the ovens warmed.
"I've taken a new job. I wanted you to hear it from me."
Priscila wiped her hands slowly. "When?"
"I'll give you four weeks. And I'll still do the Oliveira wedding cake on the twentieth, since I promised them."
For the next month Mina trained the new baker, Leandro, on the sourdough starter and wrote the feeding times on the fridge door. When a customer asked why she was leaving, she said only, "A new challenge. I've learned so much here." She never mentioned the broken mixer or the late payslips.
On her last day Priscila handed her a jar of the starter. "Come back and bake for us whenever you like."

qa.q: What did Mina promise to still do before leaving?
qa.a: The Oliveira wedding cake on the twentieth.

qa.q: What might Priscila have felt when Mina gave the news?
qa.a: Priscila was probably disappointed and a little shaken, wiping her hands slowly, but later grateful enough to hand over a jar of the starter.

qa.q: Which of Mina's choices kept the bridge open?
qa.a: Telling Priscila first and in person, giving four weeks, finishing the wedding cake, training Leandro, and not complaining to customers.

qa.q: How might Leandro experience Mina's last month?
qa.a: Leandro got real training on the starter and the feeding times on the fridge door, so Leandro can take over without guessing.

grounding: Shows a person leaving a job honestly, finishing promised work and leaving without blame.
